title: Locating-dominating sets of the regular 4-polytopes
statement: A set D of vertices is locating-dominating when every vertex outside D has a neighbour in D and no two vertices outside D have the same set of neighbours in D; the locating-domination number is the smallest size of such a set. Determine the locating-domination number for the graphs of the six regular convex 4-polytopes (the 5-cell K5; the tesseract, 16 vertices; the 16-cell, 8 vertices; the 24-cell, 24 vertices, 8-regular; the 600-cell, 120 vertices, 12-regular; the 120-cell, 600 vertices, 4-regular) and of the two E8 polytopes 3_21 (Gosset, 56 vertices, 27-regular) and 4_21 (the 240 roots of E8, 56-regular), each vertex adjacent to its nearest neighbours. First values (ours): the 5-cell 4 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 6 (exact); the 16-cell 4 (exact); the 24-cell 7 (exact); the 600-cell 20; the 120-cell 205; the Gosset polytope 3_21 9; the E8 root polytope 4_21 15. The headline cell is the 120-cell: find a certificate with value 204 or less (the counting bound 2n/(Delta + 3): >= 172 for the 120-cell), or prove 205 optimal.
submission: Text file: the vertex numbers of the set (spaces or newlines), in the checker's vertex order (the 120-cell).
score: the number of vertices in the set (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 205 for the 120-cell, best found: CP-SAT (one worker, 5 to 60 seconds) on the model of tools/polytope_sets.py, or, for zero forcing and power domination, greedy completion and pruning between rounds of fort cuts

context: Locating-dominating sets were introduced by Slater (1987) to locate a faulty processor or an intruder from the detectors that see it; for a graph of maximum degree Delta the counting bound is |D| >= 2n/(Delta + 3) (Slater), here 16 for the 600-cell, 172 for the 120-cell, 4 for 3_21 and 9 for 4_21. Exact values are known for paths, cycles, some grids and hypercubes in small dimensions; these symmetric polytope graphs are natural test cases for how close the counting bound can be.
references: P. J. Slater, Domination and location in acyclic graphs, Networks 17 (1987) 55-64
P. J. Slater, Dominating and reference sets in a graph, J. Math. Phys. Sci. 22 (1988) 445-455
H. S. M. Coxeter, Regular Polytopes (3rd ed., Dover 1973)
the vertex numbering of checkers/orig_phys.py (polytope_graph), shared by every polytope problem of the Originals

novelty.verdict: new. No locating-dominating result for the 600-cell, the 120-cell, the 24-cell or the E8 polytopes (searched with E8 and Gosset) was found on arXiv, in the journal literature (Crossref) or by web search; the known values for hypercubes and complete graphs cover only the small cells.
closest: General results on locating-dominating (the references) and its values for hypercubes, grids and products; none for these polytopes.
Our polytope problems (polytope-ising, potts3-600, cell600-idcode, cell600-forest, cell120-coil, e8-idcode, e8-resolving): other invariants of the same graphs.

All cells: the 5-cell 4 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 6 (exact); the 16-cell 4 (exact); the 24-cell 7 (exact); the 600-cell 20; the 120-cell 205; the Gosset polytope 3_21 9; the E8 root polytope 4_21 15. Bound: 172 (the counting bound 2n/(Delta + 3), for the 120-cell).
